world.h: Israelis weigh reports Netanyahu was warned
world.b: As Israel marks three years since the Oct. 7 attacks, four people with direct knowledge told NPR that Netanyahu was personally warned about a potential Hamas attack.
more: Haaretz, The New York Times and The Atlantic first reported the warnings from regional allies.
Netanyahu has denied he was warned.

world.h: Vance seeks 'meaningful' cut in Iran enrichment
world.b: Vice President JD Vance called for Iran to make a meaningful reduction in uranium enrichment capacity as part of a deal to end the war, Al Jazeera reports.
more: Experts say it may signal a softening of the earlier demand that Tehran abandon enrichment altogether.
Rubio reiterated Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon; Trump warned the war will end 'the nice way or the not-so-nice way'.

world.h: Bulgaria ends search for sunken ship's crew
world.b: Bulgarian authorities ended the search after finding no survivors from a cargo ship sunk by a drone strike off the coast on Tuesday.
more: Drones hit two commercial vessels as attacks on Black Sea shipping increase amid the Russia-Ukraine war.
Eighteen Turkish and Indian crew members were rescued from the second ship, which caught fire.

world.h: Three years since the Oct. 7 attack
world.b: Israelis gathered to mourn the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack that killed 1,200 people and saw 251 taken hostage.
more: The war it sparked has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza, including 21,000 children, Al Jazeera reports.
A ceasefire took effect Oct. 10, 2025, but attacks and killings have continued.

world.h: France suspends high school classes for week
world.b: France's prime minister suspended high school classes nationwide for the rest of the week as protesters clashed with police.
more: Authorities counted about 250,000 protesters Tuesday; organizers said closer to half a million.
Students are protesting crowded classrooms, teacher shortages and run-down buildings.

world.b: The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 4,000 in what Democracy Now! calls the fastest-growing outbreak on record.
more: Kenya confirmed its first case: a man who returned from Congo by way of Uganda died in Nairobi.
Health officials believe it began in January but was not detected until May.
Democracy Now! reports that Trump's USAID cuts have fueled the outbreak.

world.h: Puigdemont cleared to return to Spain
world.b: A Spanish judge lifted the arrest warrant for self-exiled Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, clearing his way home.
more: Spain's Constitutional Court ruled the separatist amnesty law covers his embezzlement charges.

world.b: The Parti Quebecois won the most seats in Quebec's election and will form the province's next government.
more: Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, set to become premier, promised a third referendum on leaving Canada in his first term.
It was not yet clear whether the party reached the 64 seats needed for a majority.

national.h: Tropical Storm Isaias forms, eyes Gulf Coast
national.b: Tropical Storm Isaias formed off eastern Mexico and is expected to become the Atlantic season's first hurricane before hitting the U.S. Gulf Coast later this week.
more: It had sustained winds of 40 mph, about 580 miles southwest of the Mississippi River's mouth.
Where it may make landfall was not yet known.

national.h: Texas set to execute Jamaal Howard
national.b: Texas is set to execute Jamaal Howard, 46, for the 2000 killing of convenience store clerk Vickie Swartout, in what would be the nation's 30th execution this year.
more: It is the first scheduled U.S. execution since Tennessee's failed attempt to execute Christa Pike.

national.h: Over 1,000 children buried at youth detention sites
national.b: NPR reports Georgetown University researchers are working to identify children who died at 40 reform schools and youth detention centers across the country.
more: Researchers have linked 16 families to children who died at a reform school in Cheltenham, Maryland.
The work is part of the Forgotten Children Initiative, underway since February.

national.h: Flu season is starting unusually early
national.b: Flu activity began picking up in early September, NPR reports, earlier than the usual October or November start.
more: Positive flu tests in the West have risen steadily since about the start of September, says Johns Hopkins epidemiologist Caitlin Rivers.
Emergency department visits for flu have also been rising for weeks.

national.h: Phoenix poet becomes hotline for homeless families
national.b: ProPublica reports 26-year-old advocate Austin Davis' AZ Hugs has become the unofficial emergency shelter hotline for homeless families in Maricopa County.
more: Most callers say they first tried 211, only to learn shelter could be months away.
Teachers, caseworkers, police and hospital workers have called asking for his help.

national.h: Ex-CIA official pleads guilty in $40M gold case
national.b: Former senior CIA official David Rush pleaded guilty to abusing his position to acquire Florida real estate and gold bars worth over $40 million.
more: Prosecutors say he invented a 'highly classified' program to justify buying luxury property he planned to resell.

national.h: Christa Pike awake after failed execution
national.b: Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her, is conscious and speaking in a hospital, her attorneys said.
more: Her lawyers say she suffered severe damage to her arms and is still shackled to her bed.
They called her recovery 'medically unprecedented' and expect a long one.

national.h: Oscar winner Eva Marie Saint dies at 102
national.b: Eva Marie Saint, star of 'On the Waterfront' and 'North by Northwest,' died Tuesday at 102.
more: 'On the Waterfront' was her first film, opposite Marlon Brando.

national.b: Jim Bakker, who built the 'PTL Club' televangelism empire with Tammy Faye before losing it to scandal, has died at 86.
more: His wife Lori Bakker announced his death; the cause was not immediately clear.
He had hosted 'The Jim Bakker Show' near Branson, Missouri, since 2003.

national.h: Disney, ABC take on Trump's FCC in court
national.b: ABC asked a federal judge to block the FCC's early review of its broadcast licenses, calling it unconstitutional retaliation.
more: Judge Loren AliKhan did not immediately rule.
A government lawyer argued the court lacks jurisdiction over the case.

national.h: FBI spy-hunting squads hit with deep cuts
national.b: FBI counterintelligence squads have been sharply cut nationwide even as espionage threats grow, five people familiar told NPR.
more: In many of the FBI's 56 field offices, only 50% to 60% of counterintelligence positions are filled.
In several offices the number of these squads has been cut in half.

national.h: Cornell taps Sally Yates for rape case review
national.b: Cornell named former acting US attorney general Sally Yates to lead an independent review of how it handled a former student's rape allegations.
more: The school faces outrage on campus and nationally over the case.

politics.h: Collins, Jackson clash in first Maine Senate debate
politics.b: Republican Sen. Susan Collins distanced herself from Trump, saying she is 'not exactly his favorite senator,' while Democrat Troy Jackson tied her to the president.
more: Jackson pointed to her vote to confirm Justice Brett Kavanaugh.
Democrats hope to flip the seat as they push for Senate control.

politics.h: Trump draws criticism for 'take out LA' remark
politics.b: At a Nebraska rally, Trump said Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego, calling it 'a very small price to pay.'
more: The crowd laughed and cheered; Gov. Gavin Newsom was among the critics.
The White House said he meant he wants to stop Iran from having that capability.

politics.b: The Justice Department filed 40 new cases seeking to strip citizenship from naturalized Americans, a number it calls a record.
more: Prosecutors say the targets are accused of crimes such as money laundering, child sexual abuse, visa fraud and tax evasion.
The petitions were filed from late August through early October.

politics.b: Justice Samuel Alito said the Supreme Court can do little to slow the surge in emergency appeals under Trump.
more: Emergency applications now rival the number of fully briefed cases the court hears each year.

politics.h: Abrego Garcia back in court over Liberia deportation
politics.b: Kilmar Abrego Garcia returns to federal court as the government tries to lift an order blocking his deportation to Liberia.
more: His case began when he was mistakenly deported to El Salvador last year.
His lawyers want Judge Paula Xinis to make the injunction permanent.

politics.h: Musk, Luckey Pentagon roles raise ethics worries
politics.b: A new Pentagon study of AI-powered weapons led by Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey is raising conflict-of-interest concerns.
more: Hegseth announced 'Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare' last week; Newt Gingrich also leads it.
The study is expected to take 120 days.

international.h: Kosovo elects Justina Shiroka Pula president
international.b: Kosovo lawmakers elected Justina Shiroka Pula president in the first minutes of Wednesday, ending a standoff in parliament.
more: The ruling Vetevendosje Movement and the opposition PDK agreed on her candidacy ahead of a midnight deadline.
The vote came as protests against convictions of former KLA leaders filled the streets.

international.h: Palestinian killed in West Bank olive harvest attack
international.b: Palestinian health officials say a 44-year-old man was killed and 16 others wounded when settlers, protected by Israeli forces, attacked olive harvesters near Burqa, northwest of Nablus.
more: Several of the wounded were taken to hospitals in Tulkarem and Nablus, Wafa reported.

international.h: Oman rescues crew of tanker hit in Hormuz
international.b: Oman's air force evacuated 10 crew members from a Panamanian-flagged tanker attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
more: The On Peace was struck about 17km off the Omani port of Limah, setting it on fire.

international.h: UK arrests 7th suspect in RAF Fairford case
international.b: British police arrested a 22-year-old on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts near RAF Fairford, a base hosting US warplanes.
more: It is the seventh arrest tied to the September 27 incident, which remains largely unexplained.
Police found petrol but no explosives in vans linked to five earlier suspects.

international.h: Libya's parliament ousts speaker after 12 years
international.b: Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives replaced Speaker Aguila Saleh after 12 years amid growing discontent.
more: Lawmakers elected Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi to replace him.

international.h: Sudan's al-Burhan rejects talks with RSF
international.b: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan vowed to retake 'every inch' held by the Rapid Support Forces and rejected negotiations.
more: The war has lasted three and a half years.
He spoke a day after the UN rights council called for a truce.

international.h: Tuareg rebels pull out of Mali's Kidal
international.b: Mali's Tuareg rebels say they are withdrawing from the strategic northern town of Kidal, six months after capturing it.
more: The Azawad Liberation Front called it a 'controlled withdrawal' amid air strikes by Mali's military and Russian fighters.

international.h: Kosovo police clash with protesters at parliament
international.b: Police clashed with protesters outside Kosovo's parliament over a bid to curb the Hague war crimes court.
more: Parliament ended its session without passing the changes.

international.h: UN rights council condemns Sudan attacks
international.b: The UN Human Rights Council condemned drone strikes and other attacks on civilians in Sudan and called for a truce.
more: It extended its Sudan fact-finding mission by a vote of 28 to 10, with nine abstentions.
The World Food Programme said an air attack hit a food truck in North Kordofan, killing one person.

international.b: Moroccan journalists described being targeted with Pegasus spyware as Amnesty International makes a new surveillance claim.
more: Journalist Omar Radi says Amnesty's Security Lab found Pegasus on his phone in 2020.
He says he was followed daily while investigating land dispossession; authorities deny the surveillance claims.

international.h: Yemen forces push on Houthi-held Taiz district
international.b: Yemeni government forces launched an offensive to retake the Houthi-held al-Waziiya district in Taiz, part of a push toward the Red Sea coast.
more: Houthi missiles hit Aden airport, and Saudi Arabia intercepted others aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait.
Government forces retook the port city of Mocha earlier this week.

international.h: India protests spread over voter list changes
international.b: Protests have spread across India as opposition groups demand the election chief resign over alleged voter list manipulation.
more: The 'Cockroach' youth movement, which forced the education minister out in July, is helping lead the campaign.
Protesters want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and the voter roll revision suspended.
Police detained at least 700 people in Delhi at an earlier protest.

business.h: California weighs billionaire tax for health care
business.b: A California ballot measure would levy the nation's first wealth tax on billionaires to offset federal cuts to health care, food aid and education, Marketplace reports.
more: Critics call the temporary cash a giveaway to politicians, and it's unclear how much it would raise.

business.h: Mortgage rates hit near three-year high
business.b: Mortgage rates have reached their highest level in almost three years, NPR reports, making home buying harder while prices are already high.
more: Borrowing for a car has also become more expensive.

business.h: 2 million young adults could lose Medicaid
business.b: More than 2 million people ages 19 to 24 could lose Medicaid as work requirements and more frequent checks phase in.
more: Starting Jan. 1, many states will require 80 hours a month of work, volunteering or school, or an exemption.

business.h: Emmys move to Prime Video in 2027
business.b: The Emmy Awards will stream on Prime Video starting in 2027, ending seven decades on broadcast TV.
more: The six-year deal ends the rotation among ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC.

business.h: Anduril plans $3.7B sub parts plant in Baltimore
business.b: Trump highlighted a $3.7 billion Anduril investment to build nuclear submarine components at a Baltimore-area shipyard.
more: It's one of a series of factory events as high gas prices and inflation weigh on his approval ratings.

business.h: Paramount, Warner Bros. merge into Skydance
business.b: The $111 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery is set to close Tuesday, creating a company called Skydance.
more: David Ellison becomes CEO, backed by his father Larry Ellison and investors from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and elsewhere.
The deal survived months of protests and legal and regulatory challenges in the US and Europe.

business.h: EPA rollback could hide data center plans
business.b: A proposed EPA rollback could end public notice requirements for many data centers before they are built.
more: The rule targets 'minor sources' of pollution, which many data centers fall under.
Critics say communities could be left in the dark about new air quality risks.

business.h: Faith in college value hits 50-year low
business.b: Just 31% of US adults say a college education is 'very important,' the lowest since Gallup began asking nearly 50 years ago.
more: College costs and student loans are key reasons for the drop.
The souring view comes as many colleges face an enrollment cliff.

science.h: Kagan and Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry
science.b: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the chemistry Nobel for discovering non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.
more: The committee said they solved a century-old mystery: how homochirality can emerge spontaneously.
Their work has been decisive for chemists who design reactions to make pharmaceuticals.

science.h: Neutrino hunter Francis Halzen wins Nobel
science.b: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and finding high-energy neutrinos from space.
more: The Nobel committee said his work paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.
Halzen said the news was 'a great surprise.'

sports.h: Dodgers top Braves, one win from NLCS
sports.b: The Dodgers beat the Braves 3-1 in NLDS Game 3 to take a 2-1 series lead.
more: Enrique Hernandez and Freddie Freeman homered, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto dominated again.
Braves ace Chris Sale pitched well but took the loss.

sports.h: White Sox, Rays both take 2-0 ALDS leads
sports.b: The White Sox beat the Guardians 4-3 and the Rays beat the Yankees 5-2 in Game 2 of the AL Division Series.
more: The White Sox are 4-0 this postseason, all four wins on the road.
The Yankees committed four errors behind Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler.

sports.h: Ovechkin says this season will be his last
sports.b: Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin, the NHL's career goals leader, says his 22nd season will be his final one.
more: He entered the season with 929 goals and turned 41 on September 17.

sports.h: Big Ten admits error by Michigan-WMU refs
sports.b: The Big Ten says the crew from Michigan's disputed win over Western Michigan misapplied a penalty in Nebraska's rout of Maryland.
more: Nebraska's kicker should have been allowed to retry a missed extra point after a roughing the snapper foul.

local.h: Suspects in detective stabbing caught in Mass.
local.b: Two suspects in last week's stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx were found hiding in a basement in Lynn, Massachusetts, police said.
more: D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24, were arrested by fugitive task force detectives.

local.h: Delaney Hall protest figure freed from ICE
local.b: Martin Soto, the Peruvian man at the center of summer protests at Newark's Delaney Hall, was released from ICE custody after a federal judge's order.
more: The judge cited his conditions and more than 200 days in detention.

local.h: Unlicensed Bronx doctor charged with murder
local.b: Luis Rojas Cabrera, 56, now faces a depraved indifference murder charge in the death of a 27-year-old patient during an anti-aging treatment, police say.
more: He was first arrested in July, days after Elizabeth Baron died.

local.h: ICE arrests near 40,000 across NY and NJ
local.b: ICE has made more than 19,500 arrests in New York state and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during Trump's second term, Gothamist reports from new government data.
more: The arrests are largely of Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories.

local.h: Crashes pile up on Central Park's car-free loop
local.b: Three people have died in crashes on Central Park's 6-mile loop since June as more than 100,000 people use the park each day, Gothamist reports.
more: On Monday a 71-year-old cyclist fell near 84th Street while avoiding an off-leash dog.

local.h: NYC to spend $9M on youth gender-affirming care
local.b: New York City plans to spend nearly $9 million on local groups providing gender-affirming care to minors, part of a $15 million Mamdani administration pledge.
more: It follows deals by NYU Langone and Mount Sinai with the Trump administration to stop such care for minors.

local.h: Mamdani names Rikers oversight board chair
local.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani named re-entry advocate Christopher Watler to chair the city's jail oversight board.
more: Watler has spent decades building re-entry and diversion programs.

local.h: Loophole helps Hochul, Blakeman raise millions
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul and GOP challenger Bruce Blakeman are using a quirk in state law to raise millions of dollars.
The city may expand the Cannonsville Reservoir, its third-largest drinking water source, after a drought two years ago.
more: The drought cut the city's water supply to worryingly low levels.

local.h: Legionella found in Staten Island complex
local.b: Legionella bacteria were found in a Staten Island apartment complex's water system after two residents got sick.

local.h: NYC fears migrants will skip health care
local.b: City health officials worry green card rule changes will lead some immigrants to avoid Medicaid and other benefits.

local.h: Bronx woman dies, baby critical after balcony fall
local.b: A Bronx woman died and a baby girl is in critical condition after they fell from a balcony early Tuesday, police said.
more: Someone called 911 from a building at Ollinville and Allerton avenues around 3:38 a.m.

local.h: Relief for NYC tenants losing rent vouchers
local.b: Nearly 6,300 NYC households losing federal rental aid may get to replace their vouchers and stay in their apartments.
more: HUD issued new guidance after letting the earlier aid expire caused fear among tenants and landlords.

periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 75. Southwest wind 8 to 13 mph.

periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 57. Northwest wind around 8 mph.

periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 71. West wind 7 to 11 mph.

periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 57.
